title: Pinboard snapshot cards & rollout context kit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Console customers and platform teams need a fast way to preserve, compare, and annotate operational snapshots (cost breakdowns, rollout traces, latency histograms) while they troubleshoot or run post-rollout reviews. Current dashboard cards are single-purpose and lose contextual state when users navigate between routes. Goal: design a lightweight ‘pinboard’ pattern — composable snapshot cards that capture a moment-in-time of a dashboard, include rollout metadata, and surface quick actions (annotate, share, open in trace view, revert rollout). Deliver a tokens-first component family that maps to existing console primitives so teams can adopt without ad-hoc CSS. This ticket covers research synthesis, component spec, Figma kit, accessibility review, and a small prototype for QA testing.
acceptance_criteria: Component spec includes token mapping for spacing, elevation, and status colors
Figma kit with 3 card variants (compact, detailed, timeline) and interaction flows
Prototype tested with 6 internal users and accessibility audit completed
Engineering handoff with storybook story and implementation notes in PR 1284
decisions: Use a single DOM-light card wrapper to enable drag-and-pin behavior and avoid duplicate dashboard render logic. Cards will store a compact snapshot token: {model, route, timespan, rollout_id, metric_refs} and optionally a KV cache preview. Visual language will reuse existing 'metric-chip' tokens but introduce two new tokens: pinboard-border-compact and pinboard-annotation-bg. Agreed to defer export-to-PDF to a follow-up (PM-4182).

Annotation text should include persisted markdown snippets and link to rollout timeline for context.

Expose attributes for aria-grabbed and aria-roledescription for drag interactions.
Backend: snapshot serializer API will return a compact JSON blob referenced by snapshot_id; store small preview HTML separately to avoid heavy re-rendering.
